questions.prompt: Match each rendering strategy to its description.

pairs.right: The browser builds the UI from JavaScript
The server renders full HTML per request
HTML is generated at build time and served static
The server flushes HTML in chunks as it's ready

questions.explanation: CSR renders in the browser, SSR renders per request on the server, SSG prebuilds HTML, and streaming SSR sends HTML incrementally to paint sooner.

options.text: Compressing the HTML before sending it
Downloading JavaScript to attach state and event listeners to already-rendered HTML, making it interactive
Caching the page at the edge

questions.explanation: After SSR/SSG HTML arrives, the framework hydrates it — reconstructing state and wiring up events on the existing DOM so it becomes interactive. That's main-thread work.

questions.prompt: Generating HTML at build time and serving it as static files (ideal for blogs/docs) is called ____ (three-letter abbreviation).
questions.explanation: SSG (Static Site Generation) prebuilds pages at build time; served from a CDN it gives the best TTFB and FCP for content that rarely changes.

questions.prompt: Which statements about rendering strategies are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: SSG is usually best for mostly-static content like blogs and docs
SSR puts content in the HTML earlier than CSR, but adds hydration cost
CSR shows content instantly with no JavaScript
Islands/partial hydration ship the least JavaScript

questions.explanation: SSG suits static content, SSR paints earlier than CSR but must hydrate, and islands minimize JS. CSR shows nothing until its JavaScript downloads and runs.

questions.prompt: Order what happens with server-side rendering plus hydration.

items.text: Server renders full HTML for the request
Browser receives the HTML and paints the content
Hydration attaches interactivity; the page becomes responsive

questions.explanation: SSR paints content early from server HTML, but the page isn't interactive until its JS downloads and hydration runs — the gap where INP can suffer.

questions.prompt: Is there a single best rendering strategy for all sites?

options.text: No — each trades off TTFB, first paint, JS cost, and interactivity, so you choose per content type
Yes — always use SSG, even for personalized data

questions.explanation: There's no universal winner: static content favors SSG, per-request content favors SSR/streaming, and app-like surfaces may use CSR/islands. Different pages can use different strategies.
